blocks.orig: Dar Es Salaam is the largest city and former capital of Tanzania and very vibrant! It is an important economic centre, major port and one of the fastest growing cities in the world.
blocks.html: Tanzania’s largest city and its former capital, Dar Es Salaam, is full of life! It is a key economic centre and a major port, and it ranks among the fastest growing cities on the planet.

blocks.orig: The sultan of Zanzibar founded Dar Es Salaam in 1862 on the site of the village of Mzizima. The name means “Place of Peace” in Arabic. First the city remained only a small port until the German East Africa Company established a station there in 1887. Then with the starting point for the Central Line railroad, it served as the capital of German East Africa from 1891–1916.
blocks.html: In 1862 the sultan of Zanzibar founded Dar Es Salaam where the village of Mzizima once stood. In Arabic, the name means “Place of Peace”. At first the city was no more than a small port, until the German East Africa Company set up a station there in 1887. As the starting point of the Central Line railroad, it then served as the capital of German East Africa from 1891–1916.

blocks.orig: Buildings in Dar Es Salaam often reflect the city’s colonial past and show a rich mix of architectural styles. They  include Swahili, British, German, and Asian traditions. But after the 2nd world war the city saw modernization and expansion with modern multi-storey buildings. It’s natural, nearly landlocked harbour is the outlet for most of mainland Tanzania’s agricultural and mineral exports. In addition it serves the nearby land-locked countries. Furthermore it is Tanzania’s most prominent city in arts, fashion, media, music, film and television and is a leading financial centre.
blocks.html: Much of the architecture in Dar Es Salaam reflects the city’s colonial past, with a rich blend of styles drawn from Swahili, British, German and Asian traditions. After the 2nd world war, however, the city modernised and expanded with modern multi-storey buildings. Its natural, almost landlocked harbour handles most of mainland Tanzania’s agricultural and mineral exports and serves the land-locked countries nearby as well. On top of that, Dar Es Salaam is Tanzania’s leading city for arts, fashion, media, music, film and television, and a major financial centre.

blocks.orig: With its beautiful harbour, stunning beaches, and thriving nightlife, the city has become a popular tourist destination. And the city has one of the largest market in East Africa, modern shopping malls and delicious local restaurants. In addition it also offers the opportunity to enjoy the beautiful sandy beaches that can be found on the quiet coastline to the north and south of the city. Here you can enjoy a refreshing drink and the azure blue ocean. There is something for everyone!
blocks.html: Thanks to its beautiful harbour, superb beaches and lively nightlife, the city has grown into a popular tourist destination. You will also find one of the largest markets in East Africa, modern shopping malls and delicious local restaurants. Beyond that, the quiet coastline to the north and south of the city offers beautiful sandy beaches where you can sip a cool drink and gaze at the azure blue ocean. There really is something for everyone!

blocks.orig: Dar es Salaam International Airport serves both domestic and international flights. This makes the city the leading arrival and departure point for most tourists who visit Tanzania, including the national parks for safaris and the islands.
blocks.html: Both domestic and international flights use Dar es Salaam International Airport. As a result, the city is the main point of arrival and departure for most tourists coming to Tanzania, whether they are heading for the national parks on safari or to the islands.

blocks.orig: Bongoyo Island and Mbudya Island are uninhabited islands, only a 30-minute boat ride from the mainland.
blocks.html: Just a 30-minute boat trip from the mainland lie the uninhabited islands of Bongoyo Island and Mbudya Island.

blocks.orig: Bagamoyo with its cobwebbed portals and crumbling German-era colonial buildings.
blocks.html: Bagamoyo, known for its cobwebbed portals and crumbling colonial buildings from the German era.

blocks.orig: Mikumi National Park and Saadani National Park can easily be reached.
blocks.html: Both Mikumi National Park and Saadani National Park are within easy reach.

blocks.orig: My name is Michael and I am a guide Dar Es Salaam for 18 years. The city offers everything – from historic sightseeing to shopping, beautiful beaches and even safari parks are close by!
blocks.html: I am Michael, and I have guided in Dar Es Salaam for 18 years. You can find everything in this city: historic sightseeing, shopping, beautiful beaches, and even safari parks are not far away!

blocks.orig: How long to stay? At least 1 day, but if you really want to explore Dar, even a week is not enough!
blocks.html: How long should you stay? A minimum of 1 day, though if you truly want to get to know Dar, even a week will not be enough!

Besides the city life with the largest market in East Africa, modern shopping malls and delicious local restaurants. The city also offers the opportunity to enjoy the beautiful sandy beaches that can be found on the quiet coastline to the north and south of the city!
blocks.html: The former capital of Tanzania, Dar Es Salaam, is a remarkably lively city! City life here means the largest market in East Africa, modern shopping malls and delicious local restaurants. On top of that, the quiet coastline to the north and south of the city is lined with beautiful sandy beaches for you to enjoy!

blocks.orig: The National Museum of Tanzania shows exhibits about the history and natural environment of Tanzania.
blocks.html: At the National Museum of Tanzania you can see exhibits on the history and natural environment of the country.

blocks.orig: The Askari Monument in Dar es Salaam located at the center of a roundabout on Samora Avenue. It is a memorial to the askari soldiers who fought in the British Carrier Corps in World War I.
blocks.html: The Askari Monument stands in the middle of a roundabout on Samora Avenue in Dar es Salaam. It commemorates the askari soldiers who served in the British Carrier Corps during World War I.

blocks.orig: The Azania Front Lutheran Church is a Lutheran church is among the most well-known landmarks and tourist attractions of the city and was built by the German missionaries in 1898.
blocks.html: Built by German missionaries in 1898, the Azania Front Lutheran Church is a Lutheran church that counts among the city’s best-known landmarks and tourist attractions.

blocks.orig: The Saint Joseph’s Metropolitan Cathedral is a Roman Catholic cathedral is a Gothic church that was built by the Germans between 1897 and 1902 and consecrated as a Catholic church in 1905.
blocks.html: Saint Joseph’s Metropolitan Cathedral is a Roman Catholic cathedral in Gothic style, built by the Germans between 1897 and 1902 and consecrated as a Catholic church in 1905.

blocks.orig: The Old Boma is one of the city’s oldest buildings and was built in 1866-67 by Majid bin Said, sultan of Zanzibar, close to his palace.
blocks.html: Among the oldest buildings in the city is the Old Boma, built in 1866-67 by Majid bin Said, sultan of Zanzibar, near his palace.

blocks.orig: The Uhuru Monument is a landmark monument and tourist attraction. It is a white obelisk with a replica of the Uhuru Torch mounted at its top.
blocks.html: A landmark and tourist attraction, the Uhuru Monument is a white obelisk topped with a replica of the Uhuru Torch.

blocks.orig: Kunduchi Ruins include the remnants of a late 15th-century mosque as well as Arabic graves from the 18th or 19th centuries, with some well-preserved pillar tombs plus some more recent graves.
blocks.html: At the Kunduchi Ruins you find the remains of a late 15th-century mosque together with Arabic graves from the 18th or 19th centuries, including several well-preserved pillar tombs and a few more recent graves.
